title: Barron
comment: Barron — Multilayer perceptrons with 1 hidden layer approximate functions using sums of ridge functions. Approximation rates have been stated by Andrew Barron. http://www.stat.yale.edu/~arb4/publications_files/UniversalApproximationBoundsForSuperpositionsOfASigmoidalFunction.pdf
alt_text: Barron. Multilayer perceptrons with 1 hidden layer approximate functions using sums of ridge functions. Approximation rates have been stated by Andrew Barron.

title: Wigner Ville
comment: Wigner Ville — The Wigner-Ville distribution mimics a probability distribution on the space-frequency plane. Useful to define the instantaneous frequency of a signal as the conditional expectation of frequencies. Suffers from interferences. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigner_distribution_function
alt_text: Wigner Ville. The Wigner-Ville distribution mimics a probability distribution on the space-frequency plane. Useful to define the instantaneous frequency of a signal as the conditional expectation of frequencies. Suffers from interferences.

title: Kubo Ando
comment: Kubo Ando — Classic reference: F Kubo and T Ando, Means of Positive Linear Operators, 1980, The Kubo-Ando mean generalizes geometric mean to matrices and preserves key properties (e.g. concavity and arithmetic-geometric inequality). https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF01371042.pdf
alt_text: Kubo Ando. Classic reference: F Kubo and T Ando, Means of Positive Linear Operators, 1980, The Kubo-Ando mean generalizes geometric mean to matrices and preserves key properties (e.g. concavity and arithmetic-geometric inequality).

title: Ot Interp Gaussians
comment: Ot Interp Gaussians — The Optimal Transport interpolation between two Gaussians is a Gaussian.
alt_text: Ot Interp Gaussians. The Optimal Transport interpolation between two Gaussians is a Gaussian.

title: Implicit Euler
comment: Implicit Euler — Gradient flows on metric spaces: define descent methods on non-Euclidean domains without using a gradient. A key tool studied in details by Ambrosio, Gigli and Savare. http://www.springer.com/la/book/9783764387211
alt_text: Implicit Euler. Gradient flows on metric spaces: define descent methods on non-Euclidean domains without using a gradient. A key tool studied in details by Ambrosio, Gigli and Savare.

title: Kl Ot
comment: Kl Ot — Geometry of Gaussians: Optimal Transport is flat (Euclidean) while Fisher-Rao is hyperbolic (Poincare half-plane). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information_metric
alt_text: Kl Ot. Geometry of Gaussians: Optimal Transport is flat (Euclidean) while Fisher-Rao is hyperbolic (Poincare half-plane).

title: Lasso
comment: Lasso — L2 (ridge) vs L1 (lasso) are used for the regularization of regression problems. L1 induces a sparsity prior and correctly recovers isolated spikes even with correlated designs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tikhonov_regularization
alt_text: Lasso. L2 (ridge) vs L1 (lasso) are used for the regularization of regression problems. L1 induces a sparsity prior and correctly recovers isolated spikes even with correlated designs.

title: Cfl
comment: Cfl — The Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition relates time/space step sizes for the stability of finite difference methods. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courant%E2%80%93Friedrichs%E2%80%93Lewy_condition
alt_text: Cfl. The Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition relates time/space step sizes for the stability of finite difference methods.

title: Motzkin
comment: Motzkin — Positive 1D polynomials are sums of squares. Motzkin's 2D polynomial is positive but is not a sum of squares. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive_polynomial
alt_text: Motzkin. Positive 1D polynomials are sums of squares. Motzkin's 2D polynomial is positive but is not a sum of squares.

title: Automata
comment: Automata — Cellular automata are discrete dynamical models defined by a local operator. For 3 neighbors automata, there are 256 possible rules, some more interesting than others. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automaton
alt_text: Automata. Cellular automata are discrete dynamical models defined by a local operator. For 3 neighbors automata, there are 256 possible rules, some more interesting than others.

title: Fourier Cat
comment: Fourier Cat — Fourier approximation of a cat. https://xkcd.com/26/
alt_text: Fourier Cat. Fourier approximation of a cat.

title: Burger
comment: Burger — Burgers' equation is one of the simplest nonlinear partial differential equations, with solutions exhibiting shocks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgers%27_equation
alt_text: Burger. Burgers' equation is one of the simplest nonlinear partial differential equations, with solutions exhibiting shocks.

title: Metaballs
comment: Metaballs — "Metaballs" are levelsets of mixtures of radial basis functions, which generate blobby lava-lamp-like behaviors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaballs
alt_text: Metaballs. "Metaballs" are levelsets of mixtures of radial basis functions, which generate blobby lava-lamp-like behaviors.

title: Interpolations
comment: Interpolations — Comparing 2D linear interpolation methods of order 0, 1 and 3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivariate_interpolation
alt_text: Interpolations. Comparing 2D linear interpolation methods of order 0, 1 and 3.

title: Gauss Mixtures
comment: Gauss Mixtures — A mixture of Gaussians can be represented as a weighted points cloud (actually a measure) over the mean/covariance domain. Mixture fitting is a non-convex optimization problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture_model
alt_text: Gauss Mixtures. A mixture of Gaussians can be represented as a weighted points cloud (actually a measure) over the mean/covariance domain. Mixture fitting is a non-convex optimization problem.

title: Tsp
comment: Tsp — The Travelling salesman problem is one of the most well known NP-hard problem. Concorde's solver can be used to solve exactly or approximately even large instances. http://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/tsp/index.html
alt_text: Tsp. The Travelling salesman problem is one of the most well known NP-hard problem. Concorde's solver can be used to solve exactly or approximately even large instances.

title: Schrodinger
comment: Schrodinger — Schrodinger's problem is an approximation (regularization using diffusion) of the Optimal Transport problem. https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0215
alt_text: Schrodinger. Schrodinger's problem is an approximation (regularization using diffusion) of the Optimal Transport problem.

title: Harris
comment: Harris — Harris's method is the most frequently used corner detector, based on the eigenvalues of the structure tensor. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris_Corner_Detector
alt_text: Harris. Harris's method is the most frequently used corner detector, based on the eigenvalues of the structure tensor.

title: Fixedpoints
comment: Fixedpoints — Fixed points can be attractive or repulsive depending on the derivative of the map. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixed_point_(mathematics
alt_text: Fixedpoints. Fixed points can be attractive or repulsive depending on the derivative of the map.

title: Heat Diff
comment: Heat Diff — Adding an independent Gaussian variable is the same as doing a heat diffusion on the density. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution_of_probability_distributions
alt_text: Heat Diff. Adding an independent Gaussian variable is the same as doing a heat diffusion on the density.
